base_branch.description: The base the launcher resolved from the layers below the repository's own file (config.EffectiveBaseBranch: the local config's repos.<r>.base_branch, else the project's base_branch, which a machine whose own config sets none reads from the published policy node). The runner uses it only when the fugaro.yaml at the ref does not set git.base_branch itself, which is the first layer. Absent (omitempty) for a launch whose file names the base, and for one whose resolved value is main, which is the fallback the file's own resolution already has; the launcher's skew gate omits it against a job image older than 0.12.1 rather than refusing the launch. The rules here are config.ValidBranchName's, the one validator fugaro.yaml's git.base_branch, the installation config's own top-level base_branch and the policy node's are all held to: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-' and '/', not starting with '-', '.' or '/', with no '..', '//', component starting with '.', or trailing '/', '.' or '.lock'.

title.description: The run's own job title (fugaro run --title, task.Spec.Title): the one line every surface that names the run shows (task.TitleLine). Absent for every launch that gave none, which is where the title is the task prompt's own first line. It is refused unless it is one non-empty line of at most 100 runes with no control character (task.TitleProblem, applied by the launcher and by task.Parse), which is what the pattern and maxLength here carry apart from the whitespace-only case. Needs a 0.8.5 runner, which is why a launch that sets it is gated at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's titlesSince): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without it. This property was missing until the console dependency graph's GV1.2 added its sibling: schemas/task.schema.json is additionalProperties: false, so every launch with --title wrote a task.json this schema rejected.

plan_task.description: The plan task this run works on (fugaro run --plan-task; console dependency graph plan GV1.2, decision GD5): <plan>/<task>, the id the plan's own dependency graph spells a node with. Absent for every launch that named none, which is the common case and every spec written before the field. The shape here is task.PlanTaskProblem's, applied by the launcher on write and by task.Parse on read: two or more '/'-separated elements, each starting with a letter or a digit and otherwise letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 128 bytes. Two rules of that one the pattern cannot carry are that a '.' or '..' element and a control character are refused. It is a display-only join hint: nothing authorises, admits or budgets anything by it. Needs a 0.11.2 runner, which is why a launch that sets it is gated at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's planTaskSince): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without it.

author.description: Who the launch says its commits are authored by (D604): the person who launched the run, from the repository's git.author: launcher opt-in, written into the agent's git environment as GIT_AUTHOR_NAME and GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL. Absent for every launch that names nobody, which is the common case and every launch today: nothing fills the field yet, and the run's own identity authors its commits, as it did before this field. It is a claim, not a proof, and the runner enforces nothing beyond its shape (task.AuthorProblem). A task that carries one needs a runner that reads the field: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without the author — which is why the launcher's own skew gate lands with the change that fills the field, not before it.

name.description: The author's name, as git writes it into the commit header. At most task.MaxAuthorNameLen runes, one line, with no control character and no angle bracket: it becomes a git header value, and a newline in it would forge the rest of the header block.

email.description: The author's address, as git writes it into the commit header and as a forge maps it to an account. At most task.MaxAuthorEmailLen runes (RFC 5321's maximum path length), one address: exactly one '@' with a local part before it and a domain after it, no control character and no angle bracket.

review_prs.description: Set only for a mode: review recipe (design generic-tool §3.6): the pull requests to review, 1 to 4, never together with branch/pr/previous_run.

mode.description: The resolved recipe's mode, written by the launching CLI ("artifact" today; an implement or review recipe writes nothing, so those specs are unchanged). The runner selects the run's shape from it at bootstrap, before the recipe is resolved, and cross-checks it against the resolved recipe afterwards. Needs a 0.8.0 runner, which is why an artifact launch at a job image older than that is refused at launch.

rigor.description: The rigor mode the launching CLI asked for (fugaro run --mode, docs/rigor-modes implementation-plan T1.6): the run's own request, which may raise the mode its layers resolve and never lower it (D6). Absent asks for none, which is every launch without the flag, and the run then resolves from fugaro.yaml's rigor block and the project layer alone. It is not `mode` above: that one is the recipe's mode, a different question with a different vocabulary. Needs a 0.11.1 runner, which is why a launch that would set it at an older job image is refused at launch.

paths.description: The paths the launching CLI declared this run will touch (fugaro run --path, repeatable), in the order --path named them: the runner matches them against the base branch's rigor.areas rules at D22's first moment, and a path matching no rule changes nothing. Absent for every launch that declared none. A blank path is no path (the same rule as task.InputNameBlank's, expressed as the pattern), and both bounds are task.MaxDeclaredPaths and task.MaxDeclaredPathBytes. Needs a 0.11.1 runner, the same gate `rigor` above has.

tier.description: The expectation tier of this run (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3, plan T8.1): what the run is expected to cost and take, which selects one tier of fugaro.yaml's governance.tiers. Absent is untiered — every spec written before this release, and every launch that declares no tier. fugaro run --tier writes it, and a --pr follow-up carries the tier the run it follows recorded (plan T8.1b). The vocabulary is internal/tier's and spelled exactly as it spells it: a near miss ("Trivial", "SMALL") is refused, never read as an unknown tier. It is not `rigor` above: that one is the review's depth, a different question with a different vocabulary. Needs a 0.13.0 runner: an older runner's task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields and refuses the field outright.

expected_scope.description: Roughly which files or areas the run is expected to touch (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3's expectation envelope). It is paths and never prose: nothing here reaches a prompt. Absent for every spec that declares none, and unlike `tier` above no launcher writes it yet. A blank entry is no path (the same rule as task.InputNameBlank's, expressed as the pattern), and both bounds are task.MaxDeclaredPaths and task.MaxDeclaredPathBytes. Needs a 0.13.0 runner, the same as `tier` above.

inputs.description: The files the launching CLI attached (fugaro run --attach, docs/design/artifact-runs.md §4), in the order --attach named them: each one is stored under runs/<slug>/<run>/inputs/<name> and downloaded by a mode: artifact run into <checkout>/inputs/. Absent for every launch that attached nothing. The name's own shape is checked where it becomes a filesystem path (the launcher's, then the runner's), never here. Needs a 0.8.0 runner, which is why an --attach launch at an older job image is refused at launch.

name.description: The name the file is stored and written under. A name of nothing but whitespace is no name, the same rule task.InputNameBlank applies before the launcher uploads anything.

sha256.description: The sha256 the launcher read while uploading the file. The runner verifies the object it downloads against it, so a mismatch leaves nothing at the destination.

recipe.description: The recipe the launching CLI resolved; absent means, for a first run, agent.recipe in fugaro.yaml at the ref, else default; for a follow-up, default (docs/design/recipes.md).

project_layer.description: The project layer the launching CLI read (docs/design/layered-config.md §8); the runner resolves fugaro.yaml against it. Absent: none. Needs a 0.6.0 runner.

oauth_token.description: The named Claude OAuth account this run's agent.auth: oauth workflow used (docs/design/named-oauth-tokens.md). Absent, or "default" itself, name the repository's unnamed claude-oauth-token secret; "default" is therefore never a value here, which is why the pattern alone (matching "default") is not enough. maxLength is required alongside the pattern: each of the pattern's {0,30} repetitions may consume one character or, via the dash alternative, two ("-" plus the alphanumeric it must precede), so the pattern alone admits names up to 61 characters (e.g. "a" + 30 repetitions of "-a") — config.MaxClaudeAccountNameLen (internal/config/claude_accounts.go) is 31, and this must match it exactly.

compression_off.description: task.Spec.CompressionOff, written by fugaro run --no-compression: it disables agent.compression for this run only, overriding the repository's own reviewed choice (docs/design/headroom-compression.md §4). There is no field and no flag to force compression on, so this is the only direction the override goes. Needs a 0.12.0 runner, which is why the launcher gates at launch (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's compressionSince) every launch whose task carries it: one that writes it, which --no-compression does only when the resolved configuration turns compression on, and a --pr follow-up or a --retry, which inherits it from the run it continues and so carries it even after the repository's key has been removed. task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without it.

digest_runs.description: The report run's manifest (task-governance plan T3.6, task.Spec.DigestRuns): the run IDs of the records the digest step may read, which the launching CLI listed from this repository's own runs/ prefix — the last 40 days, newest first, at most task.MaxDigestRuns of them. Absent for every launch that is not a report run, so a spec written for one is byte-identical to what the previous release wrote. The job reads each named record by name and never lists, so this list is what decides which records a run reads; the runner still refuses an ID outside its own repository's prefix (G2). It is accepted only with a recipe whose first step is digest (task.RecipeUsesDigest), the only step that reads it; a repository-sourced recipe carries its name alone, so the launcher judges the file it resolved (internal/cli/run_digest_manifest.go) and the runner resolves that name at the task's ref. Needs a 0.13.0 runner (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's digestSince, the same gate the digest step itself needs): task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task without its manifest. The launcher's image gate refuses at an older job image every launch whose task carries this field, whatever its recipe's source (internal/cli/recipes_skew.go's recipeSinceFor reads the manifest before the recipe), and one whose task carries the catalog run-digest's own text; a repository report recipe whose listing came out empty carries neither, and there the older runner refuses the digest step at bootstrap.

ab.description: The A/B pair block of a sampled launch (docs/model-ab-testing, decisions D550-D573; task.AB): which pair this run belongs to, which arm it is, and, for a challenger, the coder model it runs and the fact that it never publishes. Absent for every launch that was not sampled — which is every launch today, since nothing samples yet — so a spec without it is byte-identical to what the release before this field wrote. Both arms of one pair carry the same pair_id and differ in nothing but this block (D555): the challenger travels here and never in overrides.model, which a run with no per-role models applies to every stage and would move the reviewer both arms share, which is why an ab block and overrides.model never appear together. The vocabulary is closed, like rigor's and tier's: an unknown arm, publish or challenger_source is refused rather than read as something else. Needs a runner that knows the field: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running a challenger as a publishing run, and the launcher's own gate is what keeps a sampled launch off such a job.

pair_id.description: The pair both arms belong to: one value, written by the launcher onto both tasks, so a reader joins the two records by it. Opaque to the runner, and a blank one names no pair (the pattern is task.Spec.Validate's strings.TrimSpace rule, as the paths entries below carry it).

arm.description: Which arm this run is. The champion is the run the developer gets and publishes exactly as an unsampled run; the challenger is a shadow (task.ABArmChampion, task.ABArmChallenger).

publish.description: Present only on a challenger, and only as "none" (task.ABPublishNone): the challenger's arm never pushes, opens, updates or comments on a pull request, and the safety switch is stated rather than left to an absent field (D554). A champion publishes as it always did and carries nothing here.

challenger.description: The coder model the challenger arm runs, and the one difference between the arms (D555). It is an entry of the project layer's own challenger list, which the runner re-checks at bootstrap rather than trusting this text, so this schema does not carry that list's shape. A blank one is no model (the pattern is task.Spec.Validate's strings.TrimSpace rule).

challenger_source.description: Who named the challenger: the owner, in the project layer, never the repository's own file (D556, task.ABChallengerOwner). It is the seam D572 reserves for a later auto-flip writer; nothing reads it to pick a challenger.

review_levels.description: What the launch asks each review level to do (docs/review-levels-ab-jobmax, D724; config.ReviewLevels, read by task.Spec.ReviewLevels): l1 is the first line of review, l2 the senior round and l3 the adversarial one, and each holds the model that runs it, the effort it runs at, whether it runs at all, and what it is asked to focus on. Absent for every launch that asks nothing about levels, which is every launch today: no launcher writes the field until L1.2's --review-levels and its version gate land, so a spec without it is byte-identical to what the release before this field wrote. Written by fugaro run (L1.2); agent.levels in fugaro.yaml carries the same block (L1.3), and both are held to one set of rules (config.ReviewLevels.Validate). Needs a runner that knows the field: task.Parse decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so an older runner refuses the whole spec rather than running the task with the levels it was given.

level.description: One review level's settings (config.LevelSetting). The keys are the Go field names except `none`, which is config.LevelSetting.Off: `none` is what an owner or a launcher writes to say a level does not run, where `off: true` would read as a value rather than as a level's absence. Three of the decoder's rules are not expressible here, and are refused by config.ReviewLevels.Validate instead: an effort outside `effort`'s five values (config.Efforts; Claude Code itself warns and sends the model's default for the flag, and drops the environment variable and the settings key in silence, so nothing downstream refuses one), a focus carrying a control character, a bidi or zero-width one, a line or paragraph separator, or invalid UTF-8 (the project layer's own rule for a value out of a file, internal/config's badRune, which is why the pattern here cannot carry it), and `none: true` beside any other key, which is refused rather than read — a level that is off has no settings. The bound is a byte count while maxLength counts characters, so this schema is the looser of the two for text outside ASCII: a focus of 500 ASCII characters is at both caps, and one of 500 characters outside ASCII is over the decoder's and under this one's.

model.description: The exact model ID this level runs (config.LevelSetting.Model). Absent leaves the level on the model its own layer resolves — agent.models.reviewer for a senior level — and it is bounded by allowed_models as every other model setting is, which the runner checks rather than this schema.

effort.description: The reasoning effort this level runs at (config.LevelSetting.Effort, config.Efforts): the five values the pinned Claude Code accepts, from the least to the most, as measured against Claude Code 2.1.283 (docs/multi-model.md). Absent asks for none, which is the model's own default — that is not the same as "auto" or "unset", which are not values here. The vocabulary is closed in both directions: a value outside it is refused by config.ReviewLevels.Validate, because Claude Code would take it without a word.

none.description: True turns this level off (config.LevelSetting.Off): the level's step is not run, and the three settings beside it are refused rather than read. False, and an absent key, both mean the level runs. A level that is off under the owner's floor is refused at launch (L3.1, L1.4), which is not this schema's rule: nothing here reads the floor.

focus.description: What this level's reviewer is asked to look at, in the launcher's own words (config.LevelSetting.Focus). It is data and never a command: the runner puts it in the reviewer's prompt as quoted text, and it is never put through a shell or joined into a path. 500 is config.MaxLevelFocusBytes, which the decoder applies as a byte count as well.
